name: Mahatma Gandhi
oneLine: Proved that nonviolent resistance can defeat an empire.
whyItMatters: Gandhi showed the world that the strongest weapon is refusing to fight back. His methods inspired every major peace movement that followed.
context: Led India to independence from British colonial rule through nonviolent civil disobedience, salt marches, and hunger strikes.

name: Martin Luther King Jr.
oneLine: Dreamed of a world where people are judged by character, not color.
whyItMatters: MLK transformed the civil rights movement into a moral force that changed laws, hearts, and the course of American history — without firing a single shot.
context: Led the American civil rights movement through nonviolent protest, culminating in the Civil Rights Act of 1964.

name: Nelson Mandela
oneLine: Spent 27 years in prison and came out choosing forgiveness over revenge.
whyItMatters: Mandela proved that reconciliation is stronger than retaliation. He could have led a war — instead he built a rainbow nation.
context: After 27 years imprisoned, became South Africa's first democratically elected president and chose truth and reconciliation over vengeance.

name: Rosa Parks
oneLine: Sat down so an entire nation could stand up.
whyItMatters: One quiet act of refusal sparked the Montgomery Bus Boycott and ignited the modern civil rights movement. Proof that courage doesn't need to be loud.
context: Refused to give up her bus seat in Montgomery, Alabama in 1955, sparking a 381-day boycott.

sources.title: Rosa Parks Biography — National Women's History Museum

name: Desmond Tutu
oneLine: Taught a nation that there is no future without forgiveness.
whyItMatters: Led South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission, proving that facing painful truth together heals deeper than punishment.
context: Nobel Peace Prize winner who fought apartheid through moral persuasion and later chaired the Truth and Reconciliation Commission.

name: Malala Yousafzai
oneLine: They shot her for wanting to go to school. She kept going.
whyItMatters: Youngest Nobel Prize laureate. Survived an assassination attempt and turned her pain into a global movement for girls' education.
context: Shot by the Taliban at age 15 for advocating girls' education. Recovered and became the world's most prominent advocate for children's right to learn.

name: Wangari Maathai
oneLine: Planted 51 million trees and proved that healing the earth heals communities.
whyItMatters: Founded the Green Belt Movement, empowering rural women to plant trees, fight deforestation, and build sustainable livelihoods. First African woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize.
context: Started with one tree in her backyard in Kenya. Her movement grew to plant over 51 million trees across Africa.

name: Jane Goodall
oneLine: Lived with chimpanzees and taught humanity that we are not alone in having souls.
whyItMatters: Revolutionized our understanding of animals as feeling, thinking beings. At 90+, still travels 300 days a year fighting for nature.
context: Pioneered primate research in Tanzania, proved chimpanzees use tools and have emotions, then dedicated her life to conservation.

name: Greta Thunberg
oneLine: A teenager who looked the most powerful people on earth in the eye and said: you are failing us.
whyItMatters: Started alone with a sign outside Swedish parliament. Sparked a global youth climate movement of millions. Proved that age is no barrier to moral authority.
context: Began her school strike for climate in 2018 at age 15, catalyzing Fridays for Future and a worldwide wave of climate activism.

name: Aaron Swartz
oneLine: Believed knowledge should be free and gave his life fighting for it.
whyItMatters: Co-created RSS at 14, helped build Creative Commons and Reddit. Fought to make academic research freely accessible. His story is a reminder of what we lose when the system punishes idealism.
context: Brilliant programmer and activist who advocated for open access to information. Faced federal charges for downloading academic papers. Died at 26.

name: Tim Berners-Lee
oneLine: Invented the World Wide Web and gave it away for free.
whyItMatters: Could have been the richest person alive. Instead, he made the web open and free for everyone. That single decision changed civilization more than almost any invention in history.
context: Created the World Wide Web in 1989 at CERN and insisted it remain open, non-proprietary, and free to use.

name: Linus Torvalds
oneLine: Built the operating system the world runs on — and let everyone have it for free.
whyItMatters: Linux runs 96% of the top million web servers, all Android phones, most supercomputers, and the International Space Station. All open source. All free.
context: Created Linux as a student in 1991, starting a revolution in collaborative open-source software development.

name: Marie Curie
oneLine: Discovered radioactivity, won two Nobel Prizes, and died from her own research — because she refused to stop helping.
whyItMatters: First woman to win a Nobel Prize. First person to win two. Drove mobile X-ray units to the front lines of WWI to save soldiers. Never patented her discoveries.
context: Pioneered research on radioactivity, discovered polonium and radium, and insisted her findings belong to humanity, not profit.

name: Muhammad Ali
oneLine: The greatest fighter who ever lived — because he knew when NOT to fight.
whyItMatters: Refused to fight in Vietnam, was stripped of his title, risked prison — because he believed killing people who never harmed him was wrong. Lost everything and got it all back through principle.
context: World heavyweight champion who sacrificed his career and freedom to stand against the Vietnam War as a conscientious objector.

name: Bob Marley
oneLine: Used music to make the whole world feel like one family.
whyItMatters: Brought reggae and a message of love, resistance, and unity to every corner of the earth. Two days after being shot, played a peace concert to unite warring political factions in Jamaica.
context: From the slums of Trenchtown to a global icon. His music became the soundtrack of liberation movements across Africa, the Americas, and beyond.

name: Nonviolence
oneLine: The radical idea that not fighting back is the strongest thing you can do.
whyItMatters: Every major successful liberation movement of the 20th century used nonviolence. It works not because it's passive, but because it exposes injustice without becoming it.

name: Open Source
oneLine: What if the most powerful tools were built by everyone, owned by no one, and free for all?
whyItMatters: Open source proved that collaboration without profit motive can outperform corporate development. It runs the internet, your phone, and most of modern civilization.

name: Ubuntu
oneLine: I am because we are.
whyItMatters: An African philosophy that says a person is a person through other persons. Your humanity is tied to mine. We cannot be fully human alone. The antidote to individualism.

name: Civil Rights Movement
oneLine: Millions of ordinary people who decided they would no longer accept being treated as less than human.
whyItMatters: Changed laws, changed hearts, changed America — through sit-ins, marches, freedom rides, and an absolute refusal to accept injustice. All without firing a shot.

name: Anti-Apartheid Movement
oneLine: A global movement that said: no one is free while others are oppressed.
whyItMatters: United people across every continent against racial segregation in South Africa, proving that international solidarity can bring down even the most entrenched systems of oppression.

name: Climate Activism
oneLine: The generation that said: this is our planet too, and you're destroying it.
whyItMatters: Forced climate onto every government's agenda. Shifted trillions in investment away from fossil fuels. Led by young people who will live with the consequences.

name: Open Knowledge Movement
oneLine: The belief that all human knowledge should be freely available to all humans.
whyItMatters: Created Wikipedia, Creative Commons, open-access journals, and free educational resources. Democratized knowledge for billions of people.

name: Linux
oneLine: The invisible backbone of the modern world — built by volunteers, free for everyone.
whyItMatters: Runs 96% of web servers, all Android phones, most supercomputers, and the ISS. Proof that the most important infrastructure can be a gift, not a product.

name: The Internet
oneLine: Connected every human who has access to it — the largest shared creation in history.
whyItMatters: Democratized information, enabled global movements, connected diaspora communities, and gave a voice to billions who had none. Its best use is still being invented.

name: Reforestation
oneLine: Every tree planted is an act of faith in the future.
whyItMatters: Global reforestation efforts have planted billions of trees, restoring ecosystems, absorbing carbon, and proving that humans can heal what they've broken.
